claim: The Visitor, a particular cup, assigned errands and a reconstructed day around1900 are fictional framing.
locator: Opening states reconstruction; conditional viewer tasks throughout.
limit: No invented historical person, exact wage, recipe, tariff or dated weather reading.

claim: Traditional Iranian ice houses stored winter ice for use in summer; Meybod preserves a large domed example.
locator: Iranica opening, use/typology, final survey paragraph; PLEA pp.3579–3580.
limit: Not an assertion that all Iranian buildings used one design or that the dome dates to400BCE.

claim: Many complexes used shallow water basins and shade walls for winter ice production, then moved harvested ice into storage.
locator: Iranica ice-making sequence; METU pp.227–229 shade wall, provision pool and store.
limit: Thin-layer methods and harvesting schedules vary; no single exact depth or yield presented as universal.

claim: At Meybod the shade wall protects the pond from low winter sun; its east–west alignment places the pond on its north side.
locator: PLEA Fig.1 and p.3580; METU pp.227–228.
limit: Do not invert the wall/pond relation in maps or imply nighttime shade causes cold by itself.

claim: The plateau climate has cool winters and hot summers; modeled night-sky radiation and evaporation help water lose heat.
locator: PLEA climate data p.3580, model results p.3582 and discussion p.3585.
limit: No numerical historic temperatures, no summer instant-freezing claim; model result attributed as modern explanation.

claim: Ice was collected, transferred and insulated for seasonal storage, with adobe structures and straw/reed insulation limiting heat gain.
locator: Iranica typology/materials; PLEA storage pp.3582–3583/3586; METU pp.228–231.
limit: Do not promise zero melting or a fixed survival percentage. No claim to exact Meybod insulation thickness.

claim: Below-ground storage and massive construction shelter the ice; meltwater needs a route away at the bottom.
locator: Iranica distinction from water reservoirs; METU p.229 drain well; PLEA storage assumptions.
limit: No magicalcold generation from dome, no swimming tank, no exact underground temperature.

claim: Water supply, labor and management were part of operation; qanats could supply complexes; ownership included communal/endowed and commercial arrangements.
locator: Iranica qanat and ownership paragraphs; METU pool p.228 and distribution accounts p.225.
limit: Do not say all ice was free, equally accessible, or every house had a private ice store. Qanat diagram is generic, not surveyed Meybod route.

claim: Ice served summer cooling uses including drinks; ice-house storage itself was not a domestic food refrigerator.
locator: Iranica use/typology and Fryer discussion; PLEA introduction; METU travelers p.223/225.
limit: No exact drink recipe, no guarantee of safe direct consumption or universal availability.

claim: Operation depended on weather, supplies, insulation and upkeep; ice loss and contamination were real limits.
locator: PLEA assumptions and melt results; METU p.231 obsolescence/contamination/maintenance.
limit: No quantified historic failure rate or health outcomes; not a claim modern refrigeration and ice houses were equivalent.

claim: The process links winter production to later demand; seasonal planning is an interpretation of documented architecture and operation.
locator: Synthesis of production, storage and distribution sections.
limit: Metaphor of saving winter is explanatory; no claim heat is a substance or cold is manufactured in summer.
